notes: 200 points, six categories. Each level covers a range of points (the 'min' field). The AI proposes one score per level (Excellent = the maximum, the others the middle of the range) and the professor can type any score inside 0 to the maximum. Transcribed from the CAP3321C Final Project rubric.

criteria.name: Data Cleaning & Preparation
criteria.description: Notebook code, outputs and Markdown explanations

levels.label: Excellent
levels.description: 36-40 points. All relevant cleaning steps are performed and clearly justified. Missing values, data types, and inconsistencies are handled appropriately. Cleaning rationale is thoroughly explained in Markdown cells. Code runs without errors.

levels.label: Good
levels.description: 28-35 points. Most cleaning steps are performed correctly. Minor issues remain (e.g., one data type unconverted, incomplete explanation of a cleaning decision). Code runs with minimal warnings.

levels.label: Needs work
levels.description: 0-27 points. Significant data quality issues are left unaddressed. Little or no explanation of cleaning decisions. Code contains errors that affect downstream analysis.

criteria.name: Analysis & Visualizations
criteria.description: Notebook code, tables and the chart images saved in the notebook, checked against the assigned questions

levels.label: Excellent
levels.description: 45-50 points. All questions from the assigned section are answered with appropriate tables or plots. Visualizations are well-chosen for the data, clearly labeled (titles, axes, legends), and easy to interpret. Analysis demonstrates strong command of course skills.

levels.label: Good
levels.description: 35-44 points. Most questions are answered correctly. Visualizations are generally appropriate but may have minor labeling issues or a less-than-optimal chart type choice. Analysis is mostly sound.

levels.label: Needs work
levels.description: 0-34 points. Several questions are unanswered or answered incorrectly. Visualizations are missing, mislabeled, or inappropriate for the data. Analysis shows limited application of course skills.

criteria.name: Interpretation & Written Summaries
criteria.description: Markdown cells next to each result

levels.label: Excellent
levels.description: 27-30 points. Every question includes a clear, thoughtful written summary that demonstrates understanding of what the results mean. Observations go beyond restating numbers and provide insight and context.

levels.label: Good
levels.description: 21-26 points. Most questions include written summaries. Interpretations are generally correct but may be surface-level or simply restate the output without deeper insight.

levels.label: Needs work
levels.description: 0-20 points. Written summaries are missing for most questions or are too vague to demonstrate understanding. Little evidence that the student interpreted the results.

criteria.name: Code Quality & Organization
criteria.description: Notebook structure, headings, comments, variable names, error outputs and cell execution order

levels.label: Excellent
levels.description: 23-25 points. Notebook is well-organized with clear Markdown headings and logical flow. Code is clean, commented where needed, uses meaningful variable names, and runs top-to-bottom without errors. No leftover or unnecessary code.

levels.label: Good
levels.description: 17-22 points. Notebook is mostly organized. Code runs but may have minor issues: inconsistent formatting, sparse comments, or a few unused cells. Overall structure is followable.

levels.label: Needs work
levels.description: 0-16 points. Notebook is disorganized or difficult to follow. Code does not run cleanly, has significant errors, or lacks structure. Headings and Markdown cells are missing or misused.

criteria.name: Presentation of Findings
criteria.description: The transcript, plus the recording length for the time limit

levels.label: Excellent
levels.description: 32-35 points. Presentation is clear, well-organized, and stays within the time limit. Both partners participate in the delivery. Key findings are communicated effectively with references to visualizations. Presenters demonstrate strong understanding of their analysis.

levels.label: Good
levels.description: 24-31 points. Presentation covers the main findings and both partners participate, though delivery may be uneven. Some findings could be explained more clearly. Stays roughly within the time limit.

levels.label: Needs work
levels.description: 0-23 points. Presentation is disorganized, significantly over or under time, or only one partner presents. Key findings are unclear or not supported by the analysis. Limited evidence of understanding.

criteria.name: Collaboration & Formatting
criteria.description: Notebook header and file name (checked by code) and who did what. Whether both partners presented is judged from the video, which is not connected yet.

levels.label: Excellent
levels.description: 18-20 points. All submission guidelines are followed: header is complete, file is named correctly, partner and section responsibilities are clearly identified. Both partners contributed meaningfully.

levels.label: Good
levels.description: 14-17 points. Most guidelines are followed. Minor issues such as an incomplete header field or slightly incorrect filename. Both partners appear to have contributed.

levels.label: Needs work
levels.description: 0-13 points. Multiple submission guidelines are not followed. Header is incomplete or missing. Filename does not follow the convention. Unclear whether both partners contributed.
